text:
Ada: Quick flag — our weekly capacity forecast shows a sharp shift in token mix; long-context and streaming are up.
Sam: How sharp are we talking? numbers?
Ada: Rolling 4-week avg: total streaming requests up 62% q/q. avg context length from 1.1k -> 3.9k tokens for the top 10 customers. non-streaming requests dropped 18%.
Jules: Wow. That'll blow up KV cache and per-token GPU time. Did you re-run the throughput sims?
Ada: Ran a back-of-envelope. Assuming same request volume, projected GPU-hours increase ~47% for the next 30 days if we keep current batching + serve config.
Maria: Region note: eu-west has 12% less spare preemptible capacity this month due to other tenants — we hit soft limits last week.
InfraBot: [deploy-bot] Scheduled maintenance: eu-west GPU pool rotation in 48h. Expected 3% transient latency increase.
Sam: If eu-west drops, routing will shift more traffic to us-east which has cheaper spot capacity but higher tail latency under long contexts.
Leo: What about prioritizing non-streamed fallbacks? If streaming costs spike, we can suggest clients switch to chunked non-streaming for large docs.
Jules: That's user-visible. Also streaming reduces batching efficiency (continuous generation prevents large pack-ups). We need to model streaming as effectively higher per-token overhead.
Ada: Agreed. I ran two scenarios:
- conservative: keep routing + no client changes -> +47% GPU-hours, cost +52% (spots + prewarm labor)
- mitigated: enable aggressive prefix caching + 25% canary reroute to quantized-medium models + client chunking -> +9% GPU-hours, cost +6%
Sam: How confident are we in prefix caching gains for these workloads? They are long but highly unique documents.
Ada: Cache hit estimated 8-12% for top traffic with repeated system prompts and shared boilerplate. Not miraculous but helps.
Maria: Ops constraint: we only have 48 spare GPUs in eu-west for prewarm pools. If demand hits scenario 1, we'll need to spin up dedicated reserved capacity or throttle new signups.
Jules: Can we do a temporary rotational policy: preemptively migrate some dedicated workloads to us-central for 72h? That reduces client locality but keeps SLA.
Leo: Network cost + egress will jump. Need finance signoff.
Sam: For forecasting, we should update the 30/60/90 day model: include a token-mix multiplier. Current model assumes fixed avg tokens per request — that's broken.
Ada: I'll add a new field: streaming_ratio and median_context_length per-customer into the model. Early tests show multiplier = 1 + 0.9*(median_context_length/1000) for GPU-hours (very rough).
Maria: Also consider maintenance windows alignment — we should avoid eu-west rotation during the predicted peak on Thursday if we can defer 24h.
InfraBot: [alert] Autoscale policy triggered 3x on us-east last night at 02:17 UTC due to one heavy customer spike.
Jules: Can we add a temporary rate-limit knob per-customer for streaming throughput until we stabilize? 95th percentile cap.
Sam: Yes, but keep it opt-in for paid tiers. Risk of customer complaints.
Ada: Action items:
- Ada: push updated forecast with streaming_ratio multiplier + scenario sims by EOD (1794127200).
- Sam: prototype a temporary per-customer streaming throttle and chunked guidance in SDK (small PR by tomorrow).
- Maria: check eu-west prewarm plan and see if rotation can be moved + identify 48h extra spare GPUs across regions.
- Jules: evaluate KV cache tuning (shard size + TTL) and estimate realistic hit-rate for long docs.
- Leo: prep cost delta for finance for both scenarios.
Maria: Also looping in support to craft communication if we enable throttles.
Ada: One more thing — Optimize team, suggest a quick quantized-medium 8-bit profile for long-context to test quality/cost tradeoffs.
Leo: I'll ping Optimize.
Sam: Good. If anyone finds an acute customer causing the 3x autoscale, flag here and we'll contact their SE.
Jules: Noted. For the forecasting sheet, I'll add a column: streaming_efficiency (estimate 0.6-1.0) to reflect packing inefficiency.
Ada: Thanks all. Keeping this thread updated with the EOD sims.
InfraBot: [reminder] Next capacity sync: 1794130800 (calendar invite sent).
Maria: leaving a note — if we go the reserved path, sales needs 7 days lead time for contract.
Ada: copy. closing loop after sims. :thumbsup:
